content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "invalid_inference", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quote is verbatim and, in context, is the crux of the claim that the pruned tree is finite. The tree's nodes are finite sets D, and the selected set F_D is chosen per node; inserting c at stage k produces the different node D_k ∪ {c}, whose selected sets, children and dispensability status need not coincide with those along the original branch. The text asserts \"until the next occurrence nothing changes\" without any justification that the same F's remain selected, and the dispensability it derives is of an element of the modified set. Hence the conclusion drawn — that the ORIGINAL infinite branch contains a contracted node, contradicting pruning — does not follow from the stated premises. Nothing elsewhere in the write-up bounds minimal-transversal size or otherwise proves the finite-blocker fact, on which the entire finiteness (F) step and thus L rests."}
